subject: Dedicated autoscale fallback playbook — Tahoe Bio capacity alignment
messages:
From: Tyler Chen <tyler.chen@tahoebio.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity planning — Q2 experiments + expected burst windows

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for taking my call last week. As promised I'm sending our rough demand forecast and a short description of the burst patterns we expect during the next two quarters. Key points:
- Two weekly scheduled experiments (Tues 02:00–05:00 UTC, Thurs 18:00–22:00 UTC) that drive short 30–45m spikes up to ~12x baseline.
- Ad-hoc customer demos (1–3 events per month) where we need near-zero cold-start latency for 60–90m.
- A cautious vs aggressive runway: the attached forecast has both a baseline and a 95th percentile peak.

Can Redwood Dedicated commit to a measurable fallback/autoscale policy so these spikes don't cause failed requests? Procurement wants to understand how the contract language will reflect transient burst guarantees and any conservatism for preemptible instances.

Tyler
Director of ML Ops | Tahoe Bio
Attachments: tahoe_demand_forecast_q2-q3.xlsx
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Tyler Chen <tyler.chen@tahoebio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — Q2 experiments + expected burst windows

Tyler —

Appreciate the forecast and level-setting. High level answer: yes, we can provide a documented autoscale + fallback playbook that ties into the Dedicated contract. Practical outline below; happy to review on a call.

1) Shoulder / ephemeral pools: we recommend a small pre-warmed ephemeral slab sized to cover 3x baseline for immediate response, then an automated ramp to reserved capacity up to the committed pool. This reduces cold-start misses for demos.
2) Burst SLOs: we can commit to a 95/5 SLO for successful token delivery under specified headroom (we'll draft language).
3) Fallback hierarchy: primary reserved pool -> ephemeral pre-warm -> cross-region fallthrough (if you allow) -> compatible lower-precision model variant.
4) Eviction and preemptible behavior: we avoid using preemptible hardware for the ephemeral slab; if used for opportunistic scaling, we'll surface eviction windows and provide a study of expected retry behavior.
5) Operational guardrails: clear cooldown windows, scale-step limits, and an incident playbook (alerting + escalation to on-call).

Next steps: if you confirm the acceptance envelope (max latency during demo, allowed regions, and whether cross-region fallback is acceptable), I'll loop in Karthik to map configs to instance counts and attach a draft SLA addendum.

Would you be available Wed 16 Apr 10:00 PT for a 30m sync?

— Logan
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_initial_capacity_matrix.csv
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tyler Chen <tyler.chen@tahoebio.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — technical sizing notes

Tyler / Logan — adding a few technical constraints and recommended parameter sets so procurement sees concrete numbers:

- Baseline: Tahoe's baseline rps translates to ~8 concurrent gen sessions needing 80 GPU tokens/s on our 80-token-per-GPU accounting. For safety we plan reserved pool = baseline * 1.25 = 10 sessions.
- Ephemeral pre-warm slab: 3x baseline => target 30 sessions (~3 x reserved GPUs). This slab is always-on (small slab) and avoids cold KV cache misses.
- Autoscale policy: min=reserved_pool, target_buffer=30% headroom, scale_step=+50% capacity per 90s up to ephemeral slab, max=ephemeral_slab + reserved_pool + 2x opportunistic(spot) instances. Cooldown=120s.
- Fallback model variant: quantized 4-bit variant with same API contract; expect 10–15% throughput improvement but small quality delta — include as explicit opt-in in contract.
- Warmup strategy: proactive KV cache pre-fetch on scheduled experiment windows using a preheat job 10m before start; we can provide automation for that.

Operational notes: we will publish per-route token-level latency percentiles and a headroom meter in the Console for your SREs to watch. For billing, ephemeral slab usage can be agreed as either included headroom (monthly) or metered on the transient rate.

I can draft the numeric table into the capacity matrix Logan attached.

— Karthik
Head of Dedicated Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@tahoebio.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — confirming acceptance envelope

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of procurement/legal asks before we commit:
- We need explicit contract language that guarantees the described fallback sequence and defines the measurement window for the 95/5 SLO.
- Clarify whether ephemeral slab is billed as reserved (flat monthly) or metered; Tahoe prefers a small included headroom in the monthly fee for predictability.
- We need a short testing window (72h) post-signing to run our scheduled experiments while Redwood monitors SLOs.

If you can provide a draft SLA addendum and a DocuSign link, procurement can move quickly. Our target is to have the agreement signed by 2029-04-20 to hit the Q2 ramp.

— Sofia
VP, Platform Engineering | Tahoe Bio
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@tahoebio.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2029 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning — draft SLA addendum + next steps

Sofia —

Attached is a concise SLA addendum draft that codifies: the fallback hierarchy, the 95/5 measurement approach (5-minute rolling windows aggregated over a 24-hour period during test window), the ephemeral slab sizing, and billing options (included headroom vs metered). Link to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/tahoebiocapacity/TAH-ADD-2029

Proposed next steps:
- You review and mark up the addendum by EOD Thu 18 Apr.
- Once agreed, we'll send DocuSign; sign by 20 Apr to meet your ramp.
- After signature: schedule a 72h staging test; Redwood will run passive preheat jobs and provide a daily report during the test.

If helpful I can join procurement call tomorrow to walk through specific billing options.

— Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachments: sla_addendum_draft.pdf
